Synopsis:
J.P. Morgan and BNP Paribas revised their ECB outlooks, now forecasting an additional 25bps rate hike in December, having previously expected the tightening cycle to end. The revision is driven by persistent energy price pressures (oil above $95/bbl, Iran conflict), sticky core inflation, resilient eurozone growth, and rising second-round inflation effects. Markets have near-fully priced a September 10 hike at 99.2% probability. Both banks signal the door remains open to further tightening beyond December if inflationary pressures persist.
